categories.main_business_segments: National Retail Properties, Inc. (NNN) operates as a single business segment focused on acquiring, owning, investing in, and developing properties leased primarily to retail tenants under long-term net leases. All properties are considered part of a unified property portfolio, with no separate reportable segments disclosed.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: NNN's core business model centers on the acquisition and management of single-tenant, freestanding retail properties, typically under long-term triple-net leases where tenants are responsible for property expenses. The company employs rigorous underwriting, due diligence (including environmental assessments), and portfolio management practices to ensure stable returns and asset quality.
categories.primary_customers_markets: NNN's primary customers are retail tenants across a diverse range of industries, including convenience stores, automotive services, restaurants (full and limited service), family entertainment centers, health and fitness, and theaters. The company serves national and regional retail chains, with its largest tenant concentrations in convenience stores, automotive services, and restaurants.
categories.geographic_coverage: NNN owns 3,223 properties with approximately 32.8 million square feet of gross leasable area across 48 U.S. states. The portfolio is geographically diversified, with the largest concentrations in Texas (16.9% of annual base rent), Florida (8.6%), Ohio, Illinois, and North Carolina, and a focus on the South and Southeast regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: NNN operates as a downstream participant in the real estate supply chain, functioning as a property owner and landlord. The company leases properties directly to end-user retail tenants, providing real estate infrastructure for their operations.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: NNN's strategic focus is on investing in well-located retail real estate with long-term, net leases to high-quality tenants, aiming for stable current returns and potential capital appreciation. The company emphasizes diversification by tenant, geography, and line of trade, and maintains a disciplined acquisition and disposition strategy. While not R&D-driven, NNN invests in portfolio management, tenant credit evaluation, and ESG initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: NNN generates revenue primarily through rental income from long-term triple-net leases, where tenants pay base rent and are responsible for property operating expenses. Additional revenue streams include real estate expense reimbursements, percentage rents, and occasional gains from property dispositions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: NNN competes with other publicly traded and private real estate investment trusts (REITs), commercial developers, real estate partnerships, and institutional investors for net-lease retail properties. The company is positioned as one of the largest and most established net-lease REITs, with a long track record of dividend growth and high occupancy rates.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, NNN had total assets of $7.75 billion and annual revenues of $726 million. The company has maintained high occupancy (99%) and consistent portfolio growth, with $555 million invested in property acquisitions in 2021 and a 9.9% increase in total revenues year-over-year. NNN has increased its annual dividend for 32 consecutive years, reflecting stable growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: NNN offers investors a stable and growing income stream through a diversified portfolio of high-occupancy, long-term net-leased retail properties. Its triple-net lease structure shifts operating risks to tenants, resulting in predictable cash flows and low capital expenditure requirements. The company's disciplined investment approach, tenant and geographic diversification, and long history of dividend increases differentiate it from peers.
